USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Clique and TARGET is Vertex Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = Clique
Clique.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a clique of AT LEAST k vertices: k vertices with an
edge between every two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
always no.

TARGET = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-06xadald

    reduce(instance) -> instance

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

You may read files such as problems.py, but do not run, execute or test any code. Write reduce.py, then submit.

function.arguments:
{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-06xadald && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover.

Given a Clique instance ``{"n": n, "edges": E, "k": k}`` on graph G, build the
complement graph G' on the same vertex set and output the Vertex Cover instance
``{"n": n, "edges": E', "k": n - k}``.

Correctness
-----------
A set C is a vertex cover of G' iff V \\ C is an independent set of G'.  An
independent set in G' is exactly a clique in G.  Hence G has a clique of size
at least k iff G' has an independent set of size at least k iff G' has a vertex
cover of size at most n - k.

The edge cases line up as well:
  * k <= 0: Clique is yes; the target parameter n - k >= n, and a vertex cover
    of size at most n - k always exists (all n vertices suffice).
  * k > n: Clique is no; the target parameter n - k < 0, and Vertex Cover is
    always no for a negative budget.
  * k = 1 with n >= 1: Clique is yes; n - 1 vertices cover G' because G' has
    at least one non-edge (indeed any single vertex is an independent set).
"""

from itertools import combinations


def reduce(instance):
    """Return a Vertex Cover instance equivalent to the Clique instance."""
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # Edges of the complement graph: every non-edge of the input graph.
    original = {frozenset((u, v)) for u, v in edges}
    complement_edges = [
        [u, v] for u, v in combinations(range(n), 2) if frozenset((u, v)) not in original
    ]

    return {"n": n, "edges": complement_edges, "k": n - k}
EOF

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover.

Given a Clique instance ``{"n": n, "edges": E, "k": k}`` on graph G, build the
complement graph G' on the same vertex set and output the Vertex Cover instance
``{"n": n, "edges": E', "k": n - k}``.

Correctness
-----------
A set C is a vertex cover of G' iff V \\ C is an independent set of G'.  An
independent set in G' is exactly a clique in G.  Hence G has a clique of size
at least k iff G' has an independent set of size at least k iff G' has a vertex
cover of size at most n - k.

The edge cases line up as well:
  * k <= 0: Clique is yes; the target parameter n - k >= n, and a vertex cover
    of size at most n - k always exists (all n vertices suffice).
  * k > n: Clique is no; the target parameter n - k < 0, and Vertex Cover is
    always no for a negative budget.
  * k = 1 with n >= 1: Clique is yes; n - 1 vertices cover G' because G' has
    at least one non-edge (indeed any single vertex is an independent set).
"""

from itertools import combinations


def reduce(instance):
    """Return a Vertex Cover instance equivalent to the Clique instance."""
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # Edges of the complement graph: every non-edge of the input graph.
    original = {frozenset((u, v)) for u, v in edges}
    complement_edges = [
        [u, v] for u, v in combinations(range(n), 2) if frozenset((u, v)) not in original
    ]

    return {"n": n, "edges": complement_edges, "k": n - k}
